tools.name: lookup_nyc_building
tools.description: Finds a New York City residential building in HPD's records by borough, house number and street, and returns its registration status (valid, expired or missing), open filing violations, apartment count and Woodpecker's yearly price for it. Use when the user gives an address.

tools.name: get_nyc_building
tools.description: Returns the same facts as lookup_nyc_building for one building, by its HPD building id (the number in Woodpecker's /b/ links and on HPD Online).

tools.name: get_woodpecker_price
tools.description: The flat yearly price for a building with a given number of apartments, what the plan includes, and the renewal price. Buildings with more than 20 apartments are quoted by email.

tools.name: explain_hpd_filing_requirements
tools.description: HPD's rules in plain words: who must file the yearly property registration, the May 21 to September 1 window, who files the December bed bug report, what happens without a valid registration, and who signs. Sourced from HPD's own pages.

tools.name: open_hpd_filing_violations_by_borough
tools.description: How many NYC buildings currently have an open HPD violation for a missing property registration or a missing annual bed bug report, by borough, counted from the city's open data.

tools.name: start_woodpecker_order
tools.description: Returns the link where the owner of a given building sees the city's record and the price and pays by card. Nothing is created until the owner pays on that page.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_woodpecker_price · Private data: lookup_nyc_building, explain_hpd_filing_requirements, start_woodpecker_order · Public sink: get_woodpecker_price.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_woodpecker_price · Private data: lookup_nyc_building, explain_hpd_filing_requirements, start_woodpecker_order · Public sink: get_woodpecker_price

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
